objects.name: Close the independent-review findings on the Coulomb friction slice

physical.statement: The published Coulomb friction slice disagrees with its own declared law in four small ways (review findings F1-F4 recorded in receipt coupled_friction_20260917): the exact-rest slide-sign fallback aids impending slip instead of opposing it, the declared critical-mu hold-vs-slide falsifier is unexercised, the impact-level friction cone has no guarding assertion, and the live qualifier's scope string still claims 'No friction'.
physical.prediction: After the four fixes the frictionless frozen references stay bit-exact (the fixes touch only friction-active paths): a direct unit seam on friction_solve returns lambda_n=1, lambda_t=+0.5 for the decoupled exact-rest case (M=I, initial={-1,-2}, mu=0.5) and lambda_t=-0.5 when slipping along +t; the critical mu derived at the settled press pose (targets 20 deg/20 deg) is ~0.782 (settle bisection; descent peak ratio ~0.785), so mu=0.8 settles into stick (slip below 1e-9 m/s over the final 600 ticks) while mu=0.6 keeps sliding (tangential travel above 1e-3 m and strictly more heat than the stick trial); every tick with a friction impact impulse above 1e-15 N*s satisfies |friction impulse| <= mu*normal impulse + 1e-9; the live qualifier's returned scope names friction.

contract.bounded_outcome: Four review fixes on the already-qualified slice: F1 exact-rest fallback sign in friction_solve plus a unit-seam executable calling friction_solve directly; F2 the derived critical-mu trial pair in the native suite; F3 a per-tick native impact-cone assertion; F4 the corrected scope string in qualify_coupled_live.py. No new contact physics, no mu_s/mu_k split, no cone generalization, no live qualification run (the operator's scene is live on port 8127).
law: F1 derivation: at exact rest (slip_sign==0) the tangential residual rt = floor_t - row_t.initial is minus the free tangential acceleration along the row; rt>0 means impending slip along -t, so friction must act along +t. The slide cap is f_t = -s*mu*lambda_n with s the slip sign along t, hence the rest fallback must be s = (rt>=0 ? -1 : +1), the opposite of the shipped sign.

F2 derivation: critical mu is measured at the settled press pose (shoulder/elbow targets 20/20) by bisection on the settle predicate 'slip below 1e-9 m/s for the final 600 ticks'; the derived boundary (frozen derivation numbers: settle mu_crit 0.7820104343, descent peak ratio 0.7848445602) brackets the two native trials mu=0.6 (slide) and mu=0.8 (stick).
F3: the impact-level cone is the same |tangential impulse| <= mu*normal-impulse law the continuous stage enforces, asserted per tick whenever friction_impact_impulse_N_s exceeds 1e-15.
F4: the scope string is an under-claim fix only; the live qualifier itself is not run in this lane.
falsifiers: F1 seam: decoupled M=I, initial={-1,-2}, mu=0.5 at rest must give lambda_n=1, lambda_t=+0.5; slipping along +t must give lambda_t=-0.5; a stick case must hold |t|<=mu*n with both floors reached; a separating case must return mode 0 with zero force; the cross-coupled M={2,.5;.5,1} slide solve must satisfy row_n.projected==floor_n and the cap t==-s*mu*n to 1e-12.

F2 pair: mu=0.8 settles stick (slip below 1e-9 over the last 600 ticks); mu=0.6 slides (tangential travel above 1e-3 m) with heat strictly greater than the mu=0.8 trial. If both stick or both slide, no derived critical mu exists and this falsifier fails.
F3 cone: any tick with friction_impact_impulse_N_s above 1e-15 violating |friction impulse| <= mu*impact_impulse_N_s + 1e-9 fails the run.
Frozen controls: the frictionless references worst_gap 4.147475858029548e-07 and drop impact heat 0.06656390658451124 must remain bit-exact; mu=0 stays the frictionless world unchanged.
contract.scope: Four review fixes on the qualified Coulomb slice; no new contact capability, no live qualification run, no change to the frictionless controls.

physical.statement: Bulk reference families (reference_entity, property_assertion, geometry_asset, mapping, relationship) move into rotated shard files on both the authored side (data/authored/records/) and the compiled side, with every consumer interface preserved.
physical.prediction: After the split, rebuilding from the same authored inputs reproduces the pre-split graph_hash bit-identically; every consumer (graphify round-trip, batch re-prove, project_spec, evidence count) passes unchanged; applying Rhea afterwards keeps every repo file under 90 MB.

law: BULK_KINDS = {reference_entity, property_assertion, geometry_asset, mapping, relationship} shard; everything else (sources, work, model, doc, model_definition...) stays in the single program/store core.

Authored: build_graph loads data/authored/records/*.json shards after project_program.json; batch apply_patches routes new BULK_KINDS objects to a rotated shard (max ~24 MB each) and the rest to the program.

Compiled: CreatureGraph.save() writes the core (non-bulk objects + all relations + meta + a bulk shard manifest) to creature_graph.json and bulk objects to creature_graph.bulk_NN.json; load()/graph_from merge shards transparently; graph_hash is computed over merged content, so the hash law is unchanged.
Shard rotation is deterministic (sorted by id, packed in order), so the same content always produces the same shard files.
falsifiers: Bit-identity: the post-split rebuild's graph_hash equals the pre-split hash exactly; any drift refuses.
Consumer parity: graphify round-trip HONEST, all five batch re-proofs byte-identical, project_spec + funnel suites green, evidence 11/11.
Ceiling: after applying Rhea, every file under tools/creature_graph/data is < 90 MB; violation refuses.

objects.name: Operator dispatches the trainer-spine repair lane

physical.text: Repair the trainer spine so the batch gate can run ANY domain: the auditor's short-history shape, the beat_generator audit path, pref_selftest's seed(rng) protocol alignment, and a two-domain batch exercise. The admitted falsifier is a bounded domain sweep over every module in Chimera/core/trainables at pop=6, gens=5.
physical.selection: Operator lane brief (branch lane/trainer-repair-20260917 from 14c56162c856); tools/science_funnel/batch/train.py had recorded the auditor short-history KeyError and the pref_selftest protocol drift for exactly this repair.

objects.name: Repair the trainer spine so the batch gate runs any domain

falsifier.statement: A spine repair that still lets a trainable domain die on an internal spine error is not a repair: the bounded domain sweep must show every module in Chimera/core/trainables completing train_and_audit(pop=6, gens=5) or refusing with its own honest cause — never an internal spine TypeError/KeyError.

physical.statement: The trainer spine (core/train_loop.py train_and_audit + core/model_auditor.py audit_run) returns an audit dict of ONE shape at every history length, refuses domains that violate the documented seed(rng) / mutate(genome, rng) / measure(genome) protocol with a named refusal instead of an internal TypeError, and the batch exercise runs the canonical domain plus a second domain end to end.
physical.prediction: After the repair: (1) train_and_audit completes at every history length >= 1 with the same audit keys; (2) beat_generator and pref_selftest complete at pop=6, gens=3 and pop=6, gens=5 (both crashed before — KeyError 'stuck_metrics' on the short-history audit dict, TypeError on seed(rng) respectively); (3) the bounded sweep over every Chimera/core/trainables module at pop=6, gens=5 shows zero internal spine errors: each module completes or refuses with its own named cause (protocol violation, missing scan, missing optional GPU dependency).

law: audit_run returns the full shape (generations, total_metrics, stuck_metrics, stuck_rate, recommendation, stuck) at EVERY history length; below 5 generations it makes NO stuck-metric claim: stuck_metrics 0, stuck [], and a recommendation that says no audit was possible — never 'All metrics moving', which would be a claim.

train_and_audit probes the domain protocol (seed accepts the protocol's rng, mutate accepts (genome, rng), measure accepts (genome)) before training and raises DomainRefusal naming the domain and the violated protocol; it never leaks a raw signature TypeError.
pref_selftest.seed aligns to the documented protocol by accepting the rng and ignoring it: the fixture is a deterministic fixed point by design, so its genome is unchanged.
The batch exercise runs EXERCISE_DOMAINS = (erisaid_mirror, pref_selftest) — the documented canonical domain plus the domain this repair unblocked — and records both runs in the receipt dict.
falsifiers: DOMAIN SWEEP (bounded, per-module timeout), run by tools/science_funnel/sweep_trainer_spine.py: every module in Chimera/core/trainables completes train_and_audit(pop=6, gens=5) or refuses with its own honest cause — a Refusal/DomainRefusal, a designed domain-frame refusal (e.g. arrangement's missing-scan FileNotFoundError), or a missing optional dependency at import (GPU domains without warp/newton). Any internal spine TypeError/KeyError, any refused outcome whose exception type is not a designed refusal, or a timeout/crash without a classified cause REFUTES the repair.
not_implemented: the seven bare-seed() domains (creature, director, brain, economy, attunement, memorial, weather) keep their signatures and are refused honestly by the spine; aligning each is per-domain work
no ML quality claim: the exercise proves wiring, not policy
GPU domains stay unexercised where warp/newton are absent
